item.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description:
CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. 

  • CVE-2024-10441 Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-40217 BerriAI LiteLLM Unprotected Alternate Channel Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-90436 Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-90817 Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. 

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. 

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. 

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

CISA also recommends users take the following measures to protect themselves from social engineering attacks:

  • Do not click web links or open attachments in unsolicited email messages.
  • Refer to Recognizing and Avoiding Email Scams for more information on avoiding email scams.
  • Refer to Avoiding Social Engineering and Phishing Attacks for more information on social engineering attacks.

No known public exploitation specifically targeting these vulnerabilities has been reported to CISA at this time.

item.title: World: Crop Prospects and Food Situation Triannual Global Report No. 3, November 2026
item.description:
Country: World
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

Please refer to the attached file.

Synopsis (short abstract)

The triannual Crop Prospects and Food Situation report provides a forward-looking global analysis of cereal production, market trends and acute food security conditions, with a particular attention on low-income food-deficit countries.

FAO estimates that 41 countries/territories require external assistance for food: 31 in Africa, eight in Asia, one in Latin America and the Caribbean, and one in Europe. Persisting conflicts and insecurity remain the primary drivers of the most severe levels of acute food insecurity, while weather shocks associated with the strong El Niño event are worsening conditions in several subregions. Looking ahead, El Niño-related impacts on production are expected to remain severe into 2027 in several subregions, likely aggravating acute food insecurity further.

The report also includes FAO's latest forecast for 2026 cereal production among the Low-Income Food-Deficit Countries (LIFDCs), pegged at 126.5 million tonnes, about 2 percent above both the 2025 level and the five-year average. The increase largely reflects a strong production recovery in Asia, particularly in Near East Asia, while production among African LIFDCs is expected to remain near-average.

item.title: World: Food Price Monitoring and Analysis (FPMA) Bulletin #9, 12 November 2026
item.description:
Country: World
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

Please refer to the attached file.

Synopsis (short abstract)

Global wheat and maize export prices declined in October 2026. Wheat prices fell amid subdued import demand and improving global production prospects, while maize prices declined from their September three‑year high amid seasonal harvest pressure in the United States of America and expectations of ample supplies from South America. Expectations of easing constraints on Black Sea export flows also weighed on wheat prices, although continued logistical disruptions in the region partly offset the downward pressure. By contrast, international rice prices increased, supported by harvest delays in some exporting countries, adverse weather conditions and rising production costs. In most domestic markets monitored by FAO, staple food prices remained relatively elevated in September and October 2026. In parts of East Africa and the Near East, conflict‑related market disruptions, currency depreciation and tight supplies continued to exert upward pressure on prices. In Far East Asia, weather-related production shortfalls and high production costs contributed to the increases in staple food prices, while in Eastern Europe, the Caucasus and Central Asia, high transport and import costs continued to exert upward pressure on domestic food prices. By contrast, the arrival of new harvests improved market supplies and contributed to seasonal price declines in parts of West Africa and Central and South America. However, strong demand, delayed harvests and unfavourable production prospects continued to drive price increases in some markets. In Southern Africa, ample domestic supplies and continued intra-regional trade helped contain seasonal price increases.

item.description:

FAITS SAILLANTS

  • Malgré un contexte toujours volatil, certains mouvements humanitaires ont repris autour de Zémio.
  • Des infrastructures pour prévenir les conflits agro-pastoraux et réduire les tensions entre éleveurs et agriculteurs dans l’Ouham-Pendé.
  • 3 900 élèves reçoivent des kits scolaires à Kaga-Bandoro et M’brès.

CONTEXTE GÉNÉRAL

Préfecture du Haut-Mbomou – Sud-Est

La situation sécuritaire demeure volatile dans la région de Zémio, malgré une accalmie relative observée récemment sur certains axes routiers autour de la ville. Dans ce contexte, les acteurs humanitaires ont progressivement repris certains déplacements et activités dans les zones affectées par les restrictions de mouvement en vigueur depuis septembre dernier. Une reprise limitée de la circulation des populations civiles a également été observée sur les principaux axes concernés, tandis que le personnel des formations sanitaires périphériques a pu se rendre à Zémio pour s’approvisionner en médicaments. Aucun incident n’a été rapporté récemment sur ces itinéraires. Une organisation humanitaire a par ailleurs effectué des déplacements sur l’axe Zémio-Dembia afin de conduire des évaluations. Compte tenu de la volatilité persistante du contexte sécuritaire, les partenaires humanitaires continuent de suivre étroitement l’évolution de la situation et maintiennent les mesures de gestion des risques et de sécurité en vigueur.

BESOINS ET RÉPONSE HUMANITAIRE

Santé

Préfecture de la Haute-Kotto – Centre

Le 11 novembre 2026, le Fonds des Nations Unies pour la population (UNFPA) et son partenaire International Medical Corps (IMC) ont clôturé leur campagne de prise en charge holistique des femmes vivant avec une fistule obstétricale. Au total, 33 patientes ont bénéficié de soins spécialisés à Bria, avec un taux de réussite de 88 %. 15 autres patientes ont été confrontées à des difficultés de déplacement pour atteindre Bria depuis Ndele dans la préfecture du Bamingui-Bangoran. Afin d’améliorer l’accès à ces services dans cette préfecture, une seconde campagne de deux semaines a lieu à Ndele du 12 au 26 novembre 2026.

Multisectoriel

Préfecture de la Vakaga – Nord-Est

Le 11 novembre 2026, l’ONG COHEB, dans le cadre du projet de Travaux de haute intensité à main d’œuvre (THIMO) mis en œuvre à travers le Programme d’appui d’urgence à la stabilisation et au relèvement des réfugiés et des communautés hôtes dans le bassin du Lac Tchad (PASRRC), a procédé à une distribution monétaire au profit de 400 bénéficiaires, dont 150 réfugiés soudanais et 250 membres des communautés hôtes. A travers l’approche « travail contre rémunération », chaque bénéficiaire a reçu une assistance en espèces de 30 000 FCFA, visant à soutenir les moyens d’existence et à répondre aux besoins prioritaires des ménages vulnérables.

item.description:

Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

HIGHLIGHTS

  • Despite a still volatile context, some humanitarian movements have resumed around Zémio.
  • Infrastructure has been installed in Ouham-Pendé to help prevent agro-pastoral conflicts and reduce tensions between herders and farmers.
  • 3,900 students received school kits in Kaga-Bandoro and M’brès.

GENERAL CONTEXT

Haut-Mbomou Prefecture – South-East

The security situation remains volatile in the Zémio area, despite a relative improvement recently observed along certain roads around the town. In this context, humanitarian actors have gradually resumed some movements and activities in areas affected by movement restrictions that have been in place since September. A limited resumption of civilian movement has also been observed on the main road corridors, while staff from peripheral health facilities have been able to travel to Zémio to replenish medical supplies. No incidents have recently been reported on these routes. A humanitarian organization also conducted movements along the Zémio-Dembia axis to carry out assessments. Given the continuing volatility of the security environment, humanitarian partners are closely monitoring developments and maintaining existing security and risk-management measures.

HUMANITARIAN NEEDS AND RESPONSE

Health

Haute-Kotto Prefecture – Central

On 11 November, the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and its partner International Medical Corps (IMC) concluded their campaign providing comprehensive care for women living with obstetric fistula. A total of 33 patients received specialized treatment in Bria, with an 88 per cent success rate. 15 other patients faced transportation challenges in reaching Bria from Ndele in Bamingui-Bangoran Prefecture. To improve access to services in that area, a second two-week campaign is being conducted in Ndele from 12 to 26 November 2026.

Multi-sector

Vakaga Prefecture – North-East

On 11 November, the NGO COHEB, under a labour-intensive work project implemented through the Emergency Project to Support the Stabilization and Recovery of Refugees and Host Communities in the Lake Chad Basin (PASRRC), distributed cash assistance to 400 beneficiaries, including 150 Sudanese refugees and 250 members of host communities. Through the cash-for-work approach, each beneficiary received 30,000 CFA francs to support livelihoods and meet priority household needs.
